findings.summary: A second deploy run that lost the lock removed the running deploy's variable file because the exit trap was set before the lock; fixed in 292121f.
The already-deployed check did not require the app container to be running, so a stopped app could be reported as deployed; fixed in 292121f.
Redaction of the log lines printed after a failure leaves a tail when two secret values overlap without one containing the other, and misses a value split across two lines.
Sending the same digest again cannot repair an unhealthy release, because the swap changes nothing when the configuration is unchanged, so the run ends in exit 9.
The database image pinned in the Compose file was never brought to the server, so the first deploy could not start the database; fixed in b398821 and ec00ee8.
An image variable exported in the root shell's environment would override the digest the script writes, and the test-only path and timing hooks are also read from that environment.
A failed creation of the run folder prints the lock-held text, and a run ended by a signal prints no line from the failure table.
Release folders are never pruned, and a failed swap of the current-release link is not checked, so the success line could print after it.
Whether Systems Manager runs the script with bash, and whether an older bash would put the secret through a temporary file, are settled only on the server.

The database image pull ran before the variable file existed and with the required Compose variables unset, which real Compose refuses; fixed in ec00ee8 with an empty env file and placeholders for that call only.
The script is tested only against stub programs, so real Docker Compose behaviour, including the placeholder pull, is proven only by the human's first deploy.
The static scan for the variables the Compose file requires uses patterns that would miss a variable reached through a YAML anchor or an extends entry.
Two sessions groomed the issue minutes apart and the second overwrote the first body, because the second orchestrator did not re-read the issue's comments before launching its PM.
